claim: Over 85% of living animal species belong to the superphylum ecdysozoa.
source: Over 85% of living animal species belong to the superphylum ecdysozoa. This group includes nematodes, arthropods, tardigrades, and five other phyla (Telford et al., 2008; Aguinaldo et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to Telford et al., 2008 and Aguinaldo et al., 1997

claim: Ecdysozoa includes nematodes, arthropods, tardigrades, and five other phyla.
source: This group includes nematodes, arthropods, tardigrades, and five other phyla (Telford et al., 2008; Aguinaldo et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citations to Telford et al., 2008 and Aguinaldo et al., 1997

claim: Ecdysozoans are defined by having a common ancestor and a specialized extracellular matrix called the cuticle that covers their body.
source: They are defined by having a common ancestor and a specialized extracellular matrix that covers their body called the cuticle.
evidence: Draws from established scientific consensus about ecdysozoan characteristics

claim: The ecdysozoan cuticle is shed and regrown to accommodate juvenile growth in a process called ecdysis or molting.

claim: Nematode parasites of plants have needle-like cuticle stylets that pierce plants and act as a syringe to deposit effectors and suck out vital nutrients.
